set_aside.subject: ownership of staff login-email behavior
set_aside.text: `staff_identity` owns “the administrative recovery override, the one replacement of a login email” and hides “Email normalization”, but its Must not own clause says “Email of any kind (there is none, A10)”
set_aside.question: Does the prohibition cover only email messaging/challenges, or also the login-email normalization, lookup, uniqueness, and replacement behavior that the same module is assigned to own?
options: `staff_identity` owns login-email identity behavior but no email messaging or challenges
`staff_identity` owns no email-related behavior, requiring another owner for login-email normalization, lookup, uniqueness, and replacement
set_aside.default_guess: Interpret the prohibition as applying only to messaging and challenges, leaving login-email identity behavior in `staff_identity`.

witness.initial: An active staff account exists with normalized login email old@example.com.
events: The holder subsequently attempts login using new@example.com.
outcomes: `staff_identity` normalizes and atomically replaces the login identifier; login with new@example.com succeeds.

Because `staff_identity` must own no email of any kind and no other module is assigned the behavior, an implementer moves or omits normalization/replacement, producing a different stored identifier or making the operation unavailable.
witness.observer: The administrator and staff holder using the recovery and login API
